taxonomy:
# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

## I. By Primary Task Type

### A. Loop Drawing
*Draw a single continuous loop through the grid*

- **Masyu** – loop constrained by black/white circle rules
- **Slitherlink** – loop on grid edges constrained by number clues
- **Mid-loop** – loop where black circles are midpoints of straight segments
- **Dotchi-Loop** – loop with straight/turn constraints per region on white circles; avoids black circles
- **Moon-or-Sun** – loop alternating between moon/sun symbols across rooms
- **Nagareru** – directional loop with wind constraints
- **Suraromu** – loop starting/ending at numbered circle, passing through all gates in order
- **Yajilin** – loop with black cells placed; arrow clues indicate black cell counts

### B. Path/Connection Drawing
*Draw paths or connections (not necessarily a single loop)*

- **Numberlink** – connect pairs of identical numbers with non-crossing paths
- **Hashiwokakero** – connect island nodes with bridges (1 or 2) to form a connected network

### C. Cell Shading / Painting
*Determine which cells to shade black*

#### C1. Shading with number clues about adjacent/nearby black cells
- **Akari** – place light bulbs; numbers indicate adjacent bulb count; illumination constraints
- **Kurotto** – numbers in circles indicate sum of contiguous black cell groups touching them
- **Kurodoko** – numbers indicate count of visible white cells in four directions
- **Nurikabe** – numbers define white island sizes; black cells form connected wall with no 2×2
- **Nurimisaki** – circles mark promontories (white dead-ends); numbers indicate white line length
- **Usowan** – numbers show adjacent black cell count, but one number per room is wrong
- **Norinori** – exactly two black cells per region, each black cell part of a domino

#### C2. Shading with region/room constraints
- **Heyawake** – numbers indicate black cell count per room; connectivity and continuity rules
- **Nuritwin** – each region has exactly two same-sized shaded blocks; global connectivity
- **Sto-stone** – numbers indicate contiguous black cells per room; "gravity drop" fills bottom half
- **LITS** – shade a tetromino per region; no same-shape adjacency; connected; no 2×2
- **Nurimeizu** – shade entire rooms to create a maze from S to G with shortest-path constraints

#### C3. Shading to form specific shapes
- **Choco Banana** – black groups must be rectangles/squares; white groups must not be
- **Shakashaka** – place triangles so remaining white areas form rectangles/squares
- **Tilepaint** – shade entire tiles; diagonal-cell clues specify black cell counts in rows/columns

#### C4. Shading by eliminating duplicates
- **Hitori** – shade cells to remove duplicate numbers in rows/columns; no adjacent black cells; white connected

### D. Region Division / Partitioning
*Divide the grid into regions or blocks*

- **Shikaku** – divide into rectangles, each containing exactly one number equal to its area
- **Five Cells** – divide into pentominoes; numbers indicate surrounding block edges
- **Double Choco** – divide into blocks each containing matching white and gray sub-shapes
- **Sashigane** – divide into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends, arrows mark ends
- **Fillomino** – fill numbers and partition into polyominoes where size equals the number; no same-size adjacency

### E. Number/Symbol Placement
*Fill cells with numbers or symbols*

- **Sudoku** – place 1–9 in rows, columns, and 3×3 boxes without repetition
- **Ripple Effect** – fill rooms with 1 to N; same numbers in a line must be spaced apart
- **Makaro** – fill rooms with 1 to N; arrows in black cells point to the largest neighbor; no same-number adjacency across rooms
- **Nansuke** – place given multi-digit numbers into a crossword-style grid
- **Juosan** – fill every cell with — or |; territory clues constrain counts; run-length limits

### F. Object Placement / Movement
*Place or move specific objects on the grid*

- **Hebi** – place snakes (sequences 1–5) with no adjacency and line-of-sight restrictions
- **Evolomino** – place growing polyomino blocks along arrow paths
- **Pencils** – identify pencil shapes and draw lines from tips of specified length
- **Satogaeri** – move numbered circles so each country has exactly one; movement distance matches number
- **Yosenabe** – move circles into gray areas via straight arrows; sums must match

### G. Chained/Connected Block Identification
- **Chained Block** – identify black cell blocks with size numbers; blocks chain at corners; unique shapes per chain

---

## II. By Constraint Mechanism

### Connectivity Constraints
*White or black cells must form a connected network*
- Hitori, Nurikabe, Kurodoko, Heyawake, LITS, Nurimisaki, Nuritwin, Usowan, Nurimeizu

### No 2×2 Constraints
*No 2×2 square of same color allowed*
- Nurikabe, LITS, Nurimisaki, Nurimeizu, Sto-stone

### Adjacency Prohibition
*Shaded cells cannot touch orthogonally*
- Hitori, Usowan, Heyawake (painted cells), Yajilin, Norinori (between snakes in Hebi)

### Visibility / Line-of-Sight
*Clues reference cells visible in straight lines*
- Akari (illumination), Kurodoko (white cell count), Hebi (snake attack sight lines)

### Room/Region Number Constraints
*Numbers constrain properties within bold-bordered regions*
- Heyawake, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Sto-stone, Nuritwin, Double Choco, Five Cells, Nurimeizu

### Shape Constraints
*Specific geometric shapes required or prohibited*
- Choco Banana (rectangles required/prohibited), Shakashaka (white rectangles), Sashigane (L-shapes), LITS (tetrominoes), Shikaku (rectangles)

### Directional / Arrow Clues
- Yajilin, Makaro, Hebi, Nagareru, Evolomino, Pencils, Yosenabe, Suraromu

---

## III. By Grid Element Used for Clues

### Numbers in cells
Akari, Fillomino, Heyawake, Hitori, Kurodoko, Kurotto, Nurikabe, Shikaku, Slitherlink, Sudoku, Ripple Effect, Makaro, Five Cells, Choco Banana, Sto-stone, Usowan, Nansuke, Juosan, Chained Block, Nuritwin, Nurimisaki, Double Choco

### Circles (black or white) in cells
Masyu, Dotchi-Loop, Mid-loop, Kurotto, Nurimisaki, Satogaeri, Sashigane, Yosenabe, Hashiwokakero, Suraromu

### Arrows in cells
Yajilin, Makaro, Hebi, Nagareru, Evolomino, Pencils, Sashigane

### Symbols (moon/sun, S/G, triangles)
Moon-or-Sun, Nurimeizu, Shakashaka

### Bold-line regions/rooms
Heyawake, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Double Choco, Norinori, Nurimeizu, Nuritwin, Sto-stone, Five Cells, Satogaeri, Tilepaint, Usowan, LITS, Juosan

### Dots on grid intersections
Slitherlink

---

## IV. By Output Type

| Output | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| **Single closed loop** | Masyu, Slitherlink, Mid-loop, Dotchi-Loop, Moon-or-Sun, Nagareru, Suraromu, Yajilin |
| **Multiple paths/connections** | Numberlink, Hashiwokakero, Pencils |
| **Binary cell coloring (black/white)** | Akari, Choco Banana, Heyawake, Hitori, Kurodoko, Kurotto, LITS, Norinori, Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Nurimeizu, Nuritwin, Shakashaka, Sto-stone, Tilepaint, Usowan, Yajilin, Chained Block |
| **Grid partitioning into regions** | Shikaku, Five Cells, Double Choco, Sashigane, Fillomino |
| **Number/symbol filling** | Sudoku, Ripple Effect, Makaro, Nansuke, Juosan, Fillomino |
| **Object placement/movement** | Hebi, Evolomino, Satogaeri, Yosenabe, Akari (bulb placement) |
